actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: AutoBio is a simulation and benchmark for robotic automation in a digital biology laboratory
The autobio package installs mujoco==3.3.0 and its model/ folder holds simulation-ready lab assets and scenes in the MJCF language
The model uses radian angles, resolves its meshes from ../../assets and uses autolimits; its option element sets the implicitfast integrator, a 0.01 s timestep, an elliptic cone and impratio 10
The base body rh_base carries no joint, so the hand is fixed to the world frame
The hand has 19 hinge joints: four for the thumb, index, ring and little finger and three for the middle finger
Every joint range starts at zero; for example rh_thj1 is 0 to 2.2 rad and rh_ffj1 is 0 to 0.3 rad
Seven equality constraints couple joint pairs; the ring and little finger base joints are tied to the index base joint with polycoef '0 1' and '0 2'
The model has twelve position actuators: seven act on joints and five act on tendon transmissions
Each actuator has an explicit ctrlrange; rh_thj1 is 0 to 2.2, rh_fft1 is 0 to 0.3, and the other actuators are 0 to 1.3

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the fixed model deterministically from the model defaults; the bridge accepts a seed in cap.world.reset.v1 but does not use it, and a reset restores the model defaults, so one ctrl sequence repeats a trajectory on the same engine.  The package's fake is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the model for the 19 hinge joints, the twelve position actuators, their explicit ctrlranges and the 0.01 s option step, then moves each directly actuated joint by a placeholder fraction of the remaining distance to its control target; it computes no inertia, torque, contact, friction, equality or actuator dynamics and so produces no MuJoCo trajectory

the stand-in has no transmission model: the five tendon actuators keep their ctrl values but move no joint, and the seven equality constraints, joint damping, armature and frictionloss defaults, joint ranges and actuator force ranges are not applied
the stand-in loads no STL mesh or texture and resolves no collision or contact; the hand base is fixed and the model has no free joint
the fake reset restores zeros and ignores the reset seed; a real MjData reset restores the model's own qpos0, which this package did not inspect
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
the stand-in does not implement mj_getState/mj_setState, so a snapshot on the fake uses the bridge's time/qpos/qvel/ctrl fallback rather than MuJoCo's full integration-state snapshot
no physical DexHand021 is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware; only the right hand is served, not the card's other hand models or the vortex mixer model

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
